aiOverview.content: Cameron and Cayden Boozer are highly-touted freshman basketball players for Duke University, known for being elite recruits and sons of former NBA All-Star Carlos Boozer. Born via IVF in 2007 to be genetic matches for their older brother, Carmani, they saved his life by providing stem cells to cure his sickle cell disease. This video explains how the Boozer twins were conceived to save their older brother's life:00:59Front Office SportsYouTube• Mar 21, 2026 00:59 Key Details About the Boozer Twins Parents: Former NBA All-Star Carlos Boozer and ex-wife CeCe Boozer. Background: Born in Utah on July 18, 2007, and raised in Miami, Florida. Recruitment: Both were top-ranked five-star recruits from Columbus High School in Miami before committing to Duke. The Lifesaving Story: Their older brother, Carmani, was diagnosed with sickle cell anemia, requiring a bone marrow transplant from a matched sibling. The twins were conceived via IVF to be a perfect match, and their stem cells cured Carmani. Playing Style: Cameron is a standout forward often recognized for his scoring and rebounding, while Cayden is a skilled guard with high-level playmaking ability. 2026 March Madness: They made their tournament debut in 2026, leading the Blue Devils as freshmen. The twins have often expressed gratitude for the opportunity to not only play high-level basketball together but also to have helped their brother.
